en: The Theravāda Vinaya Mahāvibhaṅga:
The Section on Offenses Entailing Expiation (Pācittiyakaṇḍa)
The Chapter on False Speech, 8.
The Training Rule on Proclaiming What Has Occurred:
At that time, the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Vesālī in the Great Forest, in the Gabled Hall.
Now at that time, a number of bhikkhus who were friends and companions had entered the rains residence on the bank of the river Vaggumudā.

At that time, the Vajjis were suffering from a famine—it was a time of scarcity, with crops blighted by whiteheads and reduced to mere stalks, so that it was not easy to subsist by gathering gleanings.
Then it occurred to those bhikkhus: “At present, the Vajjis are suffering from a famine—it is a time of scarcity, with crops blighted by whiteheads...”
"Living by means of lot-cards, it is not easy to subsist by gathering alms and holding them out for charity.
By what means, then, might we dwell this rains retreat together in harmony, in mutual affection, without dispute, living at ease and not being distressed for lack of alms-food?
Some said: "Come, friends, let us take up work for householders. In this way, they will think to give to us."
"In this way, being united, living in harmony, and without dispute, we shall spend a comfortable rainy season and not be distressed for lack of almsfood.
Some said: "Enough, friends; what is the use of undertaking the work of householders?
Come, friends, let us carry messages for householders. In this way, they will think to give to us."
"In this way, being united, in harmony, and without dispute, we shall spend a comfortable rainy season and not be distressed for lack of almsfood.
Some said: "Enough, friends! Why should we concern ourselves with the business of householders? Why should we carry out errands for householders?
Come, friends, let us speak in praise of one another’s superhuman qualities (uttarimanussadhamma) to the householders."
‘Such-and-such a monk is an attainer of the first jhāna; such-and-such a monk is an attainer of the second jhāna;
such-and-such a monk is an attainer of the third jhāna; such-and-such a monk is an attainer of the fourth jhāna;
such-and-such a monk is a stream-enterer; such-and-such a monk is a once-returner; such-and-such a monk is a non-returner; such-and-such a monk...’
‘The Arahant! Such-and-such a bhikkhu is one of the threefold knowledge; such-and-such a bhikkhu is one possessed of the six direct knowledges!
Thus they will think of giving us [alms].
In this way we shall dwell in harmony, in mutual agreement, without dispute, and spend the rains comfortably, not being distressed for lack of almsfood.”
“Indeed, friends, it is better that we speak in praise of one another’s superhuman states (uttarimanussadhamma) among the householders.
Thereupon those monks spoke in praise of one another’s superhuman states among the householders:
“Such-and-such a monk is an attainer of the first jhāna... [and so on] ...such-and-such a monk is possessed of the six direct knowledges (chaḷabhiñña).”
Then those people thought: “It is a gain for us, it is a great fortune for us, that such bhikkhus have entered the rains residence with us;
indeed, never before have such bhikkhus entered the rains residence with us as these bhikkhus who are virtuous and of lovely character.

They did not eat such food themselves, but gave it to their parents, they gave it to their wives and children, they gave it to their slaves, laborers, and servants, they gave it to their friends and companions, and they gave it to their kinsmen and blood relations—just as the kind of food they gave to the bhikkhus.
They do not eat, taste, or drink such kinds of solid food, soft food, or drinks for themselves as they give to their mother and father,
give to their children and wives, give to their slaves, laborers, and servants, give to their friends and companions, and give to their kinsmen and blood relations—
such as those they give to the bhikkhus.
Then those monks became handsome, with plump faculties, serene facial complexions, and clear skin.
Now it is the custom for monks who have completed the rains retreat to approach the Blessed One to see him.
So, at the end of the three months after completing the rains retreat, those monks put their lodgings in order, took their bowls and robes, and set out for Vesālī.
Gradually approaching Vesālī, they went to the Great Wood, to the Gabled Hall, where the Blessed One was staying.
Having approached and paid homage to the Blessed One, they sat down to one side.
Now at that time, the monks who had completed the rains retreat in various directions were thin, coarse, ill-favored, pale and sallow, with their limbs covered in visible veins.
Now the monks from the banks of the Vaggumudā were handsome, with bright faculties, serene facial complexions, and clear skin.
It is the custom for the Blessed Buddhas to exchange greetings with visiting monks.
Then the Blessed One said this to the monks from the banks of the Vaggumudā:
“I hope, monks, that you are enduring; I hope you are getting by;
I hope you have spent the rains residence in comfort, being united, harmonious, and without dispute, and that you did not suffer from lack of almsfood?
“It is endurable, Blessed One; it is getting by, Blessed One.”
“Venerable sir, we have lived together in harmony, in mutual affection, without dispute, and we have spent the rains comfortably, without being distressed for alms.
The Tathāgatas ask when they know [the answer], and they do not ask when they know [the answer].
They ask when they perceive the right time, and they do not ask when they perceive it is not the right time.
Tathāgatas ask about what is connected with the goal, not about what is unconnected with the goal;
for Tathāgatas have severed the bridge regarding what is unconnected with the goal.
Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, question monks in two ways: “Shall we teach the Dhamma? or “Shall we lay down a training rule for the disciples?”

Then the Blessed One said this to the bhikkhus from the banks of the Vaggumudā River: “But how, bhikkhus, did you dwell together in harmony, in mutual agreement, without dispute, in comfort during the rains retreat, and without being distressed for almsfood?
Then those bhikkhus reported the matter to the Blessed One.
“Is it true, bhikkhus, that what you have told me is factual?”
“It is true, Blessed One.
The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked them:
“… How indeed, monks, can you, for the sake of the belly, speak in praise of superhuman states to one another among householders? …”
“Monks, this does not lead to the confidence of those without confidence...
And so, monks, you should recite this training rule:
‘If any monk should report a superhuman state to one who is not fully ordained, when it is true, it is an offense of expiation (pācittiya).’”
"But whoever" means whoever such a person...
"a monk" means... [as before].
...pe... this is the meaning intended here by the term "bhikkhu.
One who is not fully ordained (anupasampanna) means:
with the exception of a bhikkhu and a bhikkhunī, everyone else is called "not fully ordained."
"Superhuman state" (uttarimanussadhamma) means:

jhāna, liberation, concentration, attainment, knowledge and vision, development of the path, realization of the fruit, the abandoning of defilements, freedom of the mind from hindrances, and delight in solitude.
Regarding "jhāna":
The first jhāna, the second jhāna, the third jhāna, and the fourth jhāna.
As for liberation:
the void liberation, the signless liberation, and the desireless liberation.
Concentration means the emptiness concentration, the signless concentration, and the desireless concentration.
Attainment means...
The attainment of emptiness, the attainment of the signless, and the attainment of the desireless.
"Knowledge and vision" refers to the three true knowledges.

The development of the path consists of the four foundations of mindfulness, the four right endeavors, the four bases of psychic power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the noble eightfold path.
The realization of the fruit is—
The realization of the fruit of stream-entry, the realization of the fruit of once-returning, the realization of the fruit of non-returning, and the realization of arhatship.
The abandoning of defilements is the abandoning of lust, the abandoning of hatred, and the abandoning of delusion.
"Freedom from hindrances of the mind" means freedom of the mind from lust, freedom of the mind from hatred, and freedom of the mind from delusion.
"Delight in an empty dwelling" means:

Delight in an empty dwelling by means of the first jhāna; delight in an empty dwelling by means of the second jhāna; delight in an empty dwelling by means of the third jhāna; delight in an empty dwelling by means of the fourth jhāna.
“Should inform”:
for one who says to a person not fully ordained, “I have attained the first jhāna,” there is an offense of expiation (pācittiya).
"Should inform" means:
for one who says to a person not fully ordained, "I enter the first jhāna," there is an offense of expiation (pācittiya).
"Should inform" means...
If one says to a person who is not fully ordained, “I have attained the first jhāna,” there is an offense of expiation (pācittiya).
“Should announce” means:
if one says to a person who is not fully ordained, “We have obtained the first jhāna,” there is an offense of expiation.
"Should inform" means:
for one who says to a person not fully ordained, "I am a master of the first jhāna," there is an offense of expiation (pācittiya).
"Should inform" means...
For one who has not received full ordination, there is an offense of expiation for saying, "The first jhāna has been realized by me.
For one who announces it to one who has not received full ordination: "The second jhāna... [and so on].

For one who says, “I attained the third jhāna… the fourth jhāna; I am attaining it; I have attained it; I am a master of the fourth jhāna; I have realized the fourth jhāna,” there is an offense of expiation (pācittiya).
“Should announce” means:
To one who is not fully ordained: "The emptiness liberation...
[and so on] ...the signless liberation...
the wishless liberation..."

If one says, "I have entered, I am entering, or I have entered the emptiness concentration... the signless concentration... the desireless concentration; I am an attainer of the desireless concentration, I am master of it; the desireless concentration has been realized by me," there is an offense of expiation (pācittiya).
“Should inform” means [informing] one who is not fully ordained: “I have attained the emptiness attainment … the signless attainment …” [and so forth].

If one says, “I have entered, I am entering, or I have entered the wishless attainment; I am a possessor of, I am master of, the wishless attainment; the wishless attainment has been realized by me,” there is an offense of expiation (pācittiya). “Should he announce” means:

if one says to a person who is not fully ordained, “I have entered, I am entering, or I have entered the three knowledges (tisso vijjā); I am a possessor of, I am master of, the three knowledges; the three knowledges have been realized by me,” there is an offense of expiation.
"Should inform" means [inform] one who is not fully ordained: "The four foundations of mindfulness...
the four right endeavors... [and so forth].

If one says, “I have attained, I am attaining, I have attained the four bases of psychic power; I am a possessor and master of the four bases of psychic power; the four bases of psychic power have been realized by me,” there is an offense of expiation (pācittiya).
“Should announce” means to an unordained person: “The five faculties... [and so on]...”

If one says to a person who is not fully ordained, "I have attained, I am attaining, or I have entered into the five powers; I am a possessor and master of the five powers; the five powers have been realized by me," there is an offense of expiation (pācittiya).

If one informs [a person who is not fully ordained]: "I have attained, I am attaining, or I have entered into the seven factors of enlightenment; I am a possessor and master of the seven factors of enlightenment; the seven factors of enlightenment have been realized by me," there is an offense of expiation.
"Announces" means:
to one who is not fully ordained, [to say]—"I have attained, I am attaining, I have entered upon the Noble Eightfold Path;
I am a possessor of the Noble Eightfold Path, I abide in it; the Noble Eightfold Path has been realized by me."
For one who says, "By me," there is an offense of expiation (pācittiya).
"Should announce" means to [announce] to one who is not fully ordained: "The fruit of stream-entry... [and so forth]."

If one says, “I attained the fruit of once-returning… the fruit of non-returning… arahantship; I am attaining it; I have attained it; I am a possessor of arahantship; I am master of it; arahantship has been realized by me,” there is an offense of expiation (pācittiya).
"Should inform" means [informing] one who is not fully ordained: "Lust has been abandoned by me...
hatred has been abandoned by me... and so forth.
For one who says, "Delusion has been abandoned by me, cast out, released, relinquished, discarded, and utterly discarded," there is an offense of expiation (pācittiya).
"He should announce" means to one who is not fully ordained: "My mind is free from the hindrance of lust... [and so forth].
For one who says, “My mind is free from the hindrance of hatred… my mind is free from the hindrance of delusion,” there is an offense of expiation (pācittiya).
“Should announce” means:
To one who is not fully ordained: “In an empty hut, [I have attained] the first jhāna … the second jhāna … the third jhāna …”
If one says, "I attained the fourth jhāna; I am attaining it; I have attained it; I am a possessor of the fourth jhāna in an empty place;
I am a master of the fourth jhāna in an empty place; the fourth jhāna has been realized by me in an empty place," there is an offense of expiation (pācittiya).
"Should announce" means...
If one speaks to a person who is not fully ordained, saying: "I have entered, I am entering, or I have entered upon the first jhāna and the second jhāna;
I am a possessor and a master of the first and second jhānas;
the first and second jhānas have been realized by me," one commits an offense entailing confession (pācittiya).
“Should inform” means:

to one who is not fully ordained, [one should say]—“I attained the first jhāna and the third jhāna …pe… I attained the first jhāna and the fourth jhāna; I am attaining them; I have attained them; of the first…”

If one says, "I am an attainer of the first jhāna and an attainer of the fourth jhāna; I have realized both the first jhāna and the fourth jhāna," there is an offense of expiation (pācittiya) for one who makes such a declaration.
"Should declare" means:
To one who is not fully ordained: "The first jhāna and the emptiness liberation...
[and so on] ...the signless liberation...
the desireless liberation..."
I entered, am entering, and have entered the concentration of emptiness, the concentration of the signless, and the concentration of the desireless; and [the first jhāna].
If one says, "I am an attainer and master of the wishless concentration, and the first jhāna and the wishless concentration have been realized by me," there is an offense of expiation (pācittiya).
"Should inform" means:
To one who is not fully ordained: "I have entered, am entering, or have entered the first jhāna and the emptiness attainment...
[and so on] ...the signless attainment...
the desireless attainment; and of the first jhāna..."

If one says, “I have attained and mastered the signless attainment, and I have realized both the first jhāna and the signless attainment,” there is an offense of expiation (pācittiya) for one who makes such a declaration.
“Should declare” means:
If one says to a person who is not fully ordained: "I have attained, I am attaining, and I have entered into the first jhāna and the three true knowledges;
I am a possessor and a master of the first jhāna and the three true knowledges;
the first jhāna and the three true knowledges have been realized by me," he commits an offense of expiation (pācittiya).
"Should inform" means [inform] one who is not fully ordained: "The first jhāna and the four foundations of mindfulness...
[and so on] ...the four right efforts..."
If one says, "I have attained, I am attaining, and I have attained the four bases of psychic power;

I am a possessor and master of the first jhāna and the four bases of psychic power; the first jhāna and the four bases of psychic power have been realized by me," there is an offense of expiation (pācittiya).
"Announces" means:

to one who is not fully ordained—to announce: "I have attained, I am attaining, and I have entered upon the first jhāna and the five faculties … [as above] … and the five powers; and of the first jhāna and the five..."
If one says, "I am a possessor of the powers, I am masterful; I have realized the first jhāna and the five powers," there is an offense of expiation (pācittiya).
"Should announce" means:
If one says to a person who is not fully ordained: "I have attained, I am attaining, and I have entered upon the first jhāna and the seven factors of enlightenment;
I am a possessor and master of the first jhāna and the seven factors of enlightenment;
the first jhāna and the seven factors of enlightenment have been realized by me," he commits an offense entailing confession (pācittiya).
“He should inform” means [inform] one who is not fully ordained: “I have attained, I am attaining, and I have entered upon the first jhāna and the noble eightfold path;
I am a possessor and a master of the first jhāna and the noble eightfold path.”
If one says, "The first jhāna and the noble eightfold path have been realized by me," there is an offense of expiation (pācittiya).
"Should announce" means to an unordained person: "The first jhāna and the fruit of stream-entry... [and so forth]."
I attained, am attaining, and have attained the fruit of once-returning, the fruit of non-returning, and arhatship; and [the attainment] of the first jhāna and arhatship.
If one says, "I am a gainer [of robes], I have a dwelling; I have realized the first jhāna and arhatship," there is an offense of expiation (pācittiya).
"Should announce" means:
If one says to a person who has not received full ordination: “I attained the first jhāna; I am attaining it;

I have attained it … [and so on] … lust has been abandoned by me … hatred has been abandoned by me … delusion has been abandoned by me—it has been vomited out, released, relinquished, given up, discarded, and utterly cast away,” he commits an offense entailing confession (pācittiya).
"Should inform" means [informing] one who is not fully ordained: "I attained the first jhāna; I am attaining it; I have attained it... my mind is free from the hindrance of lust...
my mind is free from the hindrance of hatred..."
If one says, "And my mind is free from the hindrance of delusion," there is an offense of expiation (pācittiya).
"Should announce" means [to announce] to one who is not fully ordained: "The second jhāna and the third jhāna... [and so forth]."
If one says, "I have attained, I am attaining, and I have entered upon the second jhāna and the fourth jhāna;
I am a possessor and master of the second jhāna and the fourth jhāna;
the second jhāna and the fourth jhāna have been realized by me," there is an offense of expiation (pācittiya).
“Should he inform”:

if he tells one who is not fully ordained, saying, “I have attained the second jhāna and the void liberation … my mind is free from the hindrance of delusion,” he commits an offense of expiation (pācittiya).
“Should he inform”: [as above].
If one says to a person who is not fully ordained: “I have entered, am entering, and have entered upon the second jhāna and the first jhāna;
I am a possessor and a master of the second jhāna and the first jhāna;
the second jhāna and the first jhāna have been realized by me,” he commits an offense entailing confession (pācittiya). …pe…
The root text is abbreviated.
"He should inform" means [informing] one who is not fully ordained: "My mind was free from hindrances through delusion, and I attained the first jhāna; I am attaining it..."
...if he says, "My mind is free from the hindrance of delusion, I have attained the first jhāna, I am master of it;
my mind is free from the hindrance of delusion, and the first jhāna has been realized by me," he commits an offense of expiation (pācittiya). …pe…
“Should inform” means:
for one who says to a person not fully ordained, “My mind is free from the hindrance of delusion; my mind is free from the hindrance of hatred,” there is an offense of *pācittiya*.
…pe… “Should inform” means:
To one who is not fully ordained: “The first jhāna and the second jhāna and the third jhāna and the fourth jhāna,
the emptiness liberation, the signless liberation, the wishless liberation,
the emptiness concentration, the signless concentration, the wishless concentration, the emptiness attainment, the signless [attainment]...”
the wishless attainment, the three true knowledges, the four foundations of mindfulness,
the four right efforts, the four bases of psychic power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment,
the noble eightfold path, and the fruits of stream-entry, once-returning, and non-returning.
And I attained arahantship...
lust has been abandoned by me, hatred has been abandoned by me, delusion has been abandoned by me; it has been vomited out, released, relinquished, rejected, uprooted, and utterly eradicated.
My mind is free from the hindrance of lust, and my mind is free from the hindrance of hatred.
If one says, "And my mind is free from the hindrance of delusion," there is an offense of *pācittiya*.
Regarding "announces":

if one intends to say to a person who has not received full ordination, "I have attained the first *jhāna*," but instead says, "I have attained the second *jhāna*," there is an offense of *pācittiya* if the listener understands; if the listener does not understand, there is an offense of *dukkaṭa*.
"Should inform" means:
wishing to say to one who is not fully ordained, "I have attained the first jhāna," [one says] "the third jhāna...
the fourth jhāna."
the emptiness liberation,
the signless liberation,
and the desireless liberation.
the emptiness concentration,
the signless concentration,
and the desireless concentration.
the attainment of emptiness,
the attainment of the signless,
and the attainment of the desireless.
The three true knowledges,
the four foundations of mindfulness,
and the four right endeavors.
the four bases of psychic power,
the five faculties,
and the five powers;
the seven factors of enlightenment,
the noble eightfold path,
and the fruit of stream-entry.
I attained the fruit of once-returning,
the fruit of non-returning,
and arahantship …pe…

Lust has been abandoned by me, hatred has been abandoned by me, delusion has been abandoned by me; it has been vomited out, released, relinquished; it has been cast off, pulled out, and completely eradicated.
If one says, “My mind is free from the hindrance of lust;
my mind is free from the hindrance of hatred;

my mind is free from the hindrance of delusion,” there is an offense of expiation (pācittiya) for one who understands [the meaning], and an offense of wrong-doing (dukkaṭa) for one who does not understand.
“Announces”:

Desiring to say to one who is not fully ordained, “I have attained the second jhāna,” and so forth … [or] speaking while saying, “My mind is free from the hindrance of delusion,” if the listener understands, there is an offense of expiation (pācittiya); if the listener does not understand, there is an offense of wrongdoing (dukkaṭa) … and so forth.
‘Reports’ means:

if one who has not been fully ordained, wishing to say, ‘I have attained the second jhāna,’ says, ‘I have attained the first jhāna,’ then for one who understands [the lie], there is an offense of expiation (pācittiya);
for one who does not understand it, there is an offense of wrong-doing (dukkaṭa) …pe….”
The root text is abbreviated.
“He should announce” means:
one who wishes to say to a person not fully ordained, “My mind was free from hindrances through delusion,” says, “I attained the first jhāna.”
If he speaks and the other understands, there is an offense of expiation (pācittiya); if the other does not understand, there is an offense of wrong-doing (dukkaṭa) …pe… “He should inform” means:
when one wishes to say to a person who is not fully ordained, “My mind is free from the hindrance of delusion,” [but instead] says, “My mind is free from the hindrance of hatred.”
If he speaks and the other understands, there is an offense of expiation (pācittiya); if the other does not understand, there is an offense of wrong-doing (dukkaṭa) …pe….
“He should inform” means:
to one who is not fully ordained (anupasampanna)—“the first jhāna, the second jhāna, the third jhāna, and the fourth jhāna.”

If one intends to say, “I have attained jhāna… [and] my mind is free from the hindrance of hatred,” yet says instead, “My mind is free from the hindrance of delusion”—if the listener understands this, there is an offense of expiation (pācittiya);
if the listener does not understand, there is an offense of wrong-doing (dukkaṭa).
“Should inform” means:
If one who has not received full ordination intends to say, "My mind is free from the hindrance of delusion," and while wishing to speak of the second, third, and fourth jhānas...
[and so on] ...saying, "I attained the first jhāna," there is an offense of *pācittiya* if the listener understands;
if the listener does not understand, there is an offense of *dukkaṭa*. ... [and so on] ...
“He should inform” means [inform] one who is not fully ordained: “The monk who stayed in your dwelling has attained the first jhāna, is attaining it, and has attained it;
that monk is an obtainer of the first jhāna and is master of it; by that monk, the first jhāna…”
If he says, "I have realized it," there is an offense of wrong-doing (dukkaṭa).
"Should inform" means [informing] one who is not fully ordained: "The monk who stayed in your dwelling attained the second jhāna... and so forth.

If one says, "He attained the third jhāna... he attained the fourth jhāna; he enters [it], he has entered [it]; that bhikkhu is an obtainer of the fourth jhāna, he is master of it; that bhikkhu has realized the fourth jhāna," there is an offense of wrong-doing (dukkaṭa).
"Should inform" means:
To one who is not fully ordained: "The monk who lived in your dwelling attained the emptiness liberation...
[and so on] ...the signless liberation, the wishless liberation."
He entered, enters, or has entered the emptiness concentration, the signless concentration, and the desireless concentration; that bhikkhu, regarding the desireless...
If one says, "That bhikkhu is an attainer of concentration, he has mastery over it; by that bhikkhu the wishless concentration has been realized," there is an offense of wrong-doing (*dukkaṭa*).
"Should inform" means [inform] one who is not fully ordained: "The bhikkhu who dwelt in your monastery attained the attainment of emptiness... [and so forth].

If one says, "That bhikkhu has realized the signless attainment, the wishless attainment—he entered it, enters it, has entered it; he is a possessor of the wishless attainment, he has mastery over it," there is an offense of wrong-doing (dukkaṭa).
"Should inform" means:
To one who is not fully ordained: "The bhikkhu who lived in your dwelling attained the three knowledges...
[and so on] ...the four foundations of mindfulness, the four right endeavors..."
the four bases of psychic power,
the five faculties,
and the five powers;
the seven factors of enlightenment,
the noble eightfold path,
and the fruit of stream-entry.
He attained the fruit of once-returning,
the fruit of non-returning,
and arahantship … he attains … has attained … [and so on] … pe …
For that bhikkhu, lust has been abandoned,
hatred has been abandoned,
delusion has been abandoned— cast out, released, relinquished, discarded, and utterly cast away.
If he says, "That bhikkhu’s mind is free from the hindrance of lust,
his mind is free from the hindrance of hatred,
and his mind is free from the hindrance of delusion," he commits an offense of wrong-doing (dukkaṭa).
"Should inform" means [informing] one who is not fully ordained: "The bhikkhu who stayed in your dwelling attained the first jhāna in an empty hut...
[and so on] ...the second jhāna, the third jhāna, and the fourth jhāna."

“He enters [the fourth jhāna], he has entered it; that bhikkhu is an attainer of the fourth jhāna in an empty place, he is master of it; by that bhikkhu the fourth jhāna has been realized in an empty place”—for one who speaks thus, there is an offense of wrong-doing (*dukkaṭa*).
“He should announce” means:
To one who is not fully ordained: "Whoever has used your robe,
whoever has used your almsfood,
whoever has used your lodging..."

If one says, "The monk who used your medicinal requisites for the sick has attained, is attaining, or has attained the fourth jhāna in an empty hut; that monk is a master of the fourth jhāna in an empty hut;
the fourth jhāna has been realized by that monk in an empty hut," there is an offense of wrong-doing (dukkaṭa).
"Should inform" means [informing] one who is not fully ordained: "By whom your dwelling was used... [etc.
...by whom your robe was used."
The bhikkhu by whom that almsfood was consumed,
by whom that lodging was used,
and by whom those requisites for the sick— medicines and provisions— were used, [should meditate] on the fourth [jhāna] in an empty dwelling.
“He entered the fourth jhāna, he enters it, he has entered it; that bhikkhu is an obtainer of the fourth jhāna in an empty place, he is master of it;
by that bhikkhu the fourth jhāna has been realized in an empty place”—for one who speaks thus, there is an offense of wrong-doing (*dukkaṭa*).
“Should inform” means:
To one who is not fully ordained: "Because of you, [I] gave a dwelling...
[and so on]... gave a robe, gave almsfood."
If one says, "He gave lodging;
he gave medicinal requisites for the sick; that bhikkhu attained, is attaining, or has attained the fourth jhāna in an empty hut;
that bhikkhu is a gainer of the fourth jhāna in an empty hut and is master of it; by that bhikkhu the fourth jhāna has been realized in an empty hut," there is an offense of wrong-doing (dukkaṭa).
There is no offense for one who reports what is true to one who is fully ordained,
or for one who is a first-time offender.
The training rule on the false claim of supernormal powers, the eighth, is finished.
